facts.statement: Apteribis was an extinct genus of flightless birds belonging to the ibis subfamily, found only in the Hawaiian Islands.
facts.quote: Apteribis is an extinct genus of flightless birds in the ibis subfamily that was endemic to the Hawaiian Islands in the Pacific Ocean.

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Apteribis have been discovered exclusively on the islands of Maui, Lanai, and Molokai.
facts.quote: The remains of the small ibises in the genus have only been found on the islands of Maui, Lanai, and Molokai

facts.statement: The islands where Apteribis fossils were found were once part of the prehistoric landmass Maui Nui until approximately 200,000 years ago.
facts.quote: which formed part of the prehistoric island of Maui Nui until about 200,000 years ago when rising sea levels fragmented it

facts.statement: Researchers Olson and James speculate that Apteribis was originally endemic to the prehistoric island of Maui Nui.
facts.quote: Olson and James speculate that the genus was endemic to Maui Nui

facts.statement: Due to their flightlessness, Apteribis were likely susceptible to becoming trapped in lava tubes.
facts.quote: that because of their flightlessness they were susceptible to becoming trapped in lava tubes

facts.statement: Apteribis may have exerted significant predation pressure on the land snails of Maui Nui.
facts.quote: and that they may have exerted heavy predation pressure on Maui Nui's land snails

facts.statement: Analysis suggests Apteribis likely had a brown-and-beige coloration similar to a juvenile Eudocimus ibis.
facts.quote: The analyses also concluded that Apteribis may have had a brown-and-beige coloration similar to that of a juvenile Eudocimus ibis

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Apteribis may have evolved both flightlessness and its specific coloration through a process called paedomorphosis.
facts.quote: This indicates that Apteribis may have evolved both their flightlessness and their coloration through a form of paedomorphosis

facts.statement: A 2026 study found that Apteribis possessed a markedly reduced visual system compared to living ibis species.
facts.quote: A 2026 comparative anatomical study of fossil skulls found that Apteribis had a markedly reduced visual system compared with extant ibises

facts.statement: The reduction in visual structures suggests Apteribis had limited vision and was likely nocturnal.
facts.quote: The reduced development of these visual structures suggests that Apteribis had limited visual capacity and was likely nocturnal

facts.statement: Apteribis likely relied on tactile cues from its elongated bill to find prey.
facts.quote: The genus is inferred to have relied primarily on tactile cues detected through its elongated bill to locate prey

facts.statement: The prey of Apteribis included land snails and flightless crickets.
facts.quote: such as land snails and flightless crickets

facts.statement: The evolution of nocturnality in Apteribis is interpreted as an adaptation to the lack of predators in prehistoric Hawaii.
facts.quote: The evolution of nocturnality in Apteribis has been interpreted as an adaptation to the predator-free environment of prehistoric Hawaii

facts.statement: Two species of Apteribis have been formally described: A. glenos and A. brevis.
facts.quote: Two species have been described: †A. glenos Olson & Wetmore, 1976, the Moloka'i flightless ibis †A. brevis Olson & James, 1991, the Maui flightless ibis

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of A. glenos was found in the Moʻomomi dunes.
facts.quote: The holotype of A. glenos is from the Moʻomomi dunes

facts.statement: Fossil evidence from Maui suggests a third, larger species of Apteribis existed at lower elevations than A. brevis.
facts.quote: Fossil material collected on Maui indicates that a third species apparently occurred there; it was generally larger in size and occurred at lower elevations than A. brevis

facts.statement: An extremely well-preserved specimen of Apteribis from Lanai has been recovered but not yet assigned to a specific species.
facts.quote: Another, extremely well-preserved specimen has also been recovered from Lanai, though it has not yet been described to the species level

facts.statement: Apteribis belongs to the family Plataleidae.
Apteribis lived during the Late Pleistocene to the Holocene, from 0.129 million years ago until the present.
facts.quote: Time range: Late Pleistocene to Holocene (0.129 to 0 million years ago)
